evals.prompt: Quiz me on arXiv 2401.12345, one question at a time.
evals.expected_output: Confirms the paper, generates a question bank via document-reader on first use (each question tagged type:question with an anchor), asks one question at a time waiting for an answer, gives anchor-grounded feedback, records each result via review_schedule.py, and writes/updates a type:recap note at the end.
expectations: Searches for an existing type:question bank for this paper before generating a new one
Dispatches document-reader to generate the bank if none exists, rather than writing questions itself from claimed memory of the paper
Each generated question note includes an anchors entry with an exact_text_quote or comparable location
Asks only one question before waiting for a response, not multiple at once
Does not reveal the correct answer before the user responds
Feedback after each answer references the question's stored anchor rather than a full re-explanation
Calls review_schedule.py record with correct/partial/incorrect after each answer
At the end, creates or updates a single type:recap note for this paper automatically, without asking whether to save it

evals.expected_output: With no paper named and nothing established in context, asks which paper to use rather than guessing, and does not enter review mode since a paper was implied (just not named).
expectations: Does not invent or assume a specific paper without confirmation
Asks the user which paper to quiz on
Does not call research_notes_search for type:question notes across all papers (that would be review mode) before a paper is identified
Treats this as named-paper mode pending confirmation, not review mode

evals.expected_output: Enters review mode: searches for every type:question note (project-scoped), computes due-ness via review_schedule.py due, and quizzes only the due ones, most-overdue first, potentially spanning multiple papers.
expectations: Does not ask which single paper to quiz, since no paper was named and the phrasing is review-shaped
Calls research_notes_search scoped to skill:quiz-me and type:question, not to one specific paper
Calls review_schedule.py due with the collected note ids to determine the actual queue
If no questions are due, says so plainly and offers named-paper mode instead of fabricating a review session
Does not write or update a type:recap note during review mode

evals.prompt: Before you quiz me on arXiv 2401.12345, can you refetch it? A new version came out and I want to be quizzed on the updated content.
evals.expected_output: Regenerates the question bank because the paper was explicitly refetched to a newer version, rather than reusing the existing (now potentially anchor-invalid) bank.
expectations: Recognizes the explicit refetch-to-newer-version request as a reason to regenerate the bank, not just reuse the existing one
Dispatches document-reader again for the refreshed content and regenerated questions/anchors
Does not quiz from the stale pre-existing bank's anchors before the regeneration completes

evals.prompt: Quiz me on the paper titled 'Attention Is All You Need'.
evals.expected_output: Treats the title as not directly resolvable — runs a search step (per discuss's Search/Select) to resolve it to a canonical identifier before proceeding to named-paper mode.
expectations: Does not treat the raw title as a usable identifier for research_notes_search's canonical_identifier filter
Runs a provider search to resolve the title to a canonical identifier first
Proceeds to named-paper mode's question-bank check only after resolving the identifier
